messages:
samir (New Hire): hey everyone, starting Monday in the US (CA). quick onboarding questions: 1) when does medical/HSA eligibility kick in if i start mid-month? 2) is 401(k) match immediate or after probation? 3) i paid for a moving storage unit before my start date  can i submit that for reimbursement? also my commuter pre-tax account isn't visible in the payroll portal.
claire (People Ops): welcome Samir! :wave: short answers: medical eligibility is effective the 1st of the month after 30 days for mid-month starts. HSA eligibility depends on plan selection and HSA election; if you enroll in the HSA-eligible plan and we receive elections before payroll cutoff it should start the next payroll run after coverage effective date. 401(k) match starts after 3 months per policy. please upload moving/storage invoices to the HR portal and tag as "relocation". i'll check commuter acct visibility.
jordan (Benefits): hi Samir  for HSA, you must elect HSA at benefits enrollment and confirm you are not enrolled in other disqualifying coverage. contributions begin the first payroll after your coverage effective date. i'll DM you the HSA quickstart guide.
samir (New Hire): uploaded storage_receipt.pdf and moving_agreement.pdf to portal. ticket HR-EXP-2330 created. added note: "pre-start expenses - please advise taxable treatment"
expenses-bot: Uploads received. Ticket HR-EXP-2330 created. Please include employee-id and preferred bank last 4 for reimbursement. Processing ETA 1-2 pay cycles after approval.
alex (Payroll): saw HR-EXP-2330. Reimbursements for pre-start moving/storage are evaluated case-by-case; if marked as employer reimbursable we'll process gross reimbursement. If considered taxable relocation benefit, it will be taxed and shown on your payslip. If receipts approved before payroll cutoff (Fri 10:00 PT) it goes in the next cycle; otherwise the following. Commuter pre-tax account needs your transit card number to be linked  can you DM that to me?
samir (New Hire): thanks all. one more: my first pay stub shows state SDI/CA SDI deductions which seem high  is that normal for partial month?
claire (People Ops): CA SDI is withheld per state rules; partial month calculations can look odd on the first stub because of pro-rated taxable wages and benefit pre-tax elections. Jordan can share an example stub. if you want us to review your first stub after payday, drop it here (redact SSN) and Payroll will take a look. welcome aboard :tada:
